family_title: Composition, merging, routing, mixtures and adapter generation

methods.name: Model Soups
methods.full_name: Model soups (uniform / greedy weight averaging of fine-tuned models)
methods.paper_title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
methods.formula_latex: W^{\mathrm{soup}}=\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal{S}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}W_i=W_0+\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal{S}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\Delta W_i,\ \ \mathcal{S}\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\};\ \text{uniform soup: }\mathcal{S}=\{1,\dots,N\};\ \text{greedy soup: add models in order of validation accuracy, keep }i\text{ only if held-out accuracy does not drop};\ \text{all }W_i\text{ frozen, nothing trained}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(post-hoc average of }N\text{ fine-tuned models sharing one pre-trained initialization)}
methods.locus: all parameters of fully fine-tuned models that share a pre-trained initialization
methods.structure: Equal-weight barycentre (convex combination) of N points in weight space that share the base point W_0; the greedy soup is the barycentre of a validation-selected subset.
methods.mergeable_reason: The soup is a single weight vector of the original architecture, so inference costs exactly one model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free); a soup of a single model returns that model.
methods.key_idea: Models fine-tuned from the same pre-trained weights with different hyper-parameters tend to lie in one low-error basin, so averaging their weights gives ensemble-like accuracy and robustness at single-model cost.
methods.results_note: A greedy soup of fine-tuned ViT-G/14 models reached 90.94% ImageNet top-1, above the best single model of the sweep (90.78%).

relations.note: uniform soup = W_0 + (1/N) sum_i tau_i, i.e. task arithmetic with lambda = 1/N
plain averaging is Fisher merging with identity precision (isotropic merging)
AdapterSoup applies the soup recipe to adapter parameters only

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2203.05482 (Wortsman, 2022) matches; ICML 2022 per arXiv comment and Semantic Scholar. Uniform/greedy soup recipes (greedy: add models in decreasing validation accuracy, keep if held-out accuracy does not drop) and 90.94% vs 90.78% ImageNet top-1 confirmed in the PDF (Table 1).

methods.name: Fisher Merging
methods.full_name: Fisher-weighted averaging
methods.paper_title: Merging Models with Fisher-Weighted Averaging
methods.formula_latex: W^{\star}_{[p]}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}\,W_{i,[p]}}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}}\ \ (\text{per coordinate }p),\quad F_i=\mathbb{E}_{x}\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x)}\big[(\nabla_{\theta}\log p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x))^{2}\big],\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_i\lambda_i=1;\ \text{models frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one diagonal Fisher estimate per model, same size as the model)}
methods.locus: all shared parameters of models fine-tuned from the same initialization (task heads excluded)
methods.structure: Per-coordinate precision-weighted mean: the maximizer of \sum_i\lambda_i\log\mathcal{N}(\theta;\theta_i,F_i^{-1}) under a diagonal Laplace approximation of each posterior; isotropic averaging is the case F_i=I.
methods.mergeable_reason: The output is one set of weights for the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: View merging as maximizing the joint likelihood of the models' posteriors; using each model's diagonal Fisher information as its posterior precision lets every coordinate be dominated by the model that is most certain about it.
methods.results_note: Fisher merging beats isotropic averaging for robust fine-tuning and model ensembling and is competitive with intermediate-task transfer and domain-adaptive pre-training at much lower cost.

relations.note: reduces to uniform averaging when every F_i = I
both are closed-form weighted means; RegMean weights by input Gram matrices instead of Fisher diagonals
TIES reports gains over Fisher merging

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2111.09832 (Matena, 2021); NeurIPS 2022 confirmed in papers.nips.cc 2022 listing. Per-coordinate Fisher-weighted mean, lambda_i >= 0 with sum 1 (Sec. 2.2) and isotropic merging as the F=I case (Sec. 2.1) confirmed.

methods.name: RegMean
methods.full_name: Regression Mean (dataless knowledge fusion)
methods.paper_title: Dataless Knowledge Fusion by Merging Weights of Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W^{\star}=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}W_i\tilde G_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tilde G_i\Big)^{-1}=\arg\min_{W}\sum_i\|X_iW^{\top}-X_iW_i^{\top}\|_F^2\ (\text{with regularization}),\ G_i=X_i^{\top}X_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}},\ \tilde G_i=\alpha G_i+(1-\alpha)\operatorname{diag}(G_i);\ \text{non-linear-layer weights simply averaged}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(stores one }d_{in}\times d_{in}\text{ Gram matrix per linear layer per model)}
methods.locus: every linear layer (embeddings and biases averaged)
methods.structure: Layer-wise least-squares merge: the merged linear map is the Gram-weighted matrix mean of the individual maps; equals simple averaging when all G_i are equal, and the off-diagonal shrinkage \alpha (\approx0.9) acts as a pull toward the individual weights.
methods.mergeable_reason: Produces one weight matrix per layer of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free, closed form).
methods.key_idea: Merge each linear layer so that on every model's own training inputs it reproduces that model's outputs as closely as possible; this regression has a closed form that needs only inner-product statistics of the inputs, not the data itself.
methods.results_note: Across GLUE-style merging settings RegMean significantly outperforms Fisher-weighted averaging and model ensembling baselines and can preserve or improve individual-model performance without training data.

relations.note: activation-Gram weighting vs Fisher weighting

same layer-wise activation-matched least-squares merge operator (RegMean Eq. 1 with alpha = 1); Mix-of-Show solves it by gradient descent on activations sampled from each concept LoRA, RegMean in closed form with off-diagonal shrinkage alpha
standard baseline pair in merging benchmarks

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2212.09849 (Jin, 2022); ICLR 2023 per arXiv comment. Closed form W_M = (sum G~_i)^-1 sum G~_i W_i (paper uses h = xW, transposed here), G~ = alpha G + (1-alpha) diag(G), alpha = 0.9 (0.1 for T5), and simple averaging of embeddings and biases confirmed (Sec. 3, Alg. 1).
corrections: relations: sharpened the 'equivalent-to mix-of-show' note. The two methods share the merge objective, but Mix-of-Show drops the alpha shrinkage and solves it with gradients on self-generated activations.

methods.name: Task Arithmetic
methods.full_name: Task arithmetic with task vectors
methods.paper_title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(weights, combination_type='svd' | 'cat' | 'linear'): 'svd' sums the weighted dense deltas exactly and then truncates them to svd_rank by SVD, 'cat' is exact at rank sum r_i, and 'linear' mixes the A and B factors (an approximation with cross terms); low-level operator peft.utils.merge_utils.task_arithmetic
methods.formula_latex: \tau_i=\theta_i-\theta_0\ \ (\text{per matrix }\Delta W_i=W_i-W_0);\quad \theta_{\mathrm{new}}=\theta_0+\lambda\,\tau_{\mathrm{new}},\ \ \tau_{\mathrm{new}}\in\Big\{\textstyle\sum_i\tau_i\ (\text{addition}),\ -\tau\ (\text{negation}),\ \tau_C+(\tau_B-\tau_A)\ (\text{analogy})\Big\};\ \lambda\text{ tuned on held-out data; no training}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one scalar }\lambda\text{ chosen on validation data)}
methods.locus: all parameters shared between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models
methods.structure: Vector-space operations (sum, negation, analogy) on displacement vectors from the common base point \theta_0; the edited model is \theta_0 plus a linear combination of task vectors.
methods.mergeable_reason: The edited model is a single weight vector of the original architecture; only element-wise operations on weights are used.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free); \lambda=0 recovers the pre-trained model and \lambda=1 with one task vector recovers that fine-tuned model.
methods.key_idea: A fine-tuning run defines a direction in weight space; adding such task vectors builds multi-task models, negating one makes the model forget a task or behaviour, and analogies transfer skills to tasks with little data.
methods.results_note: Adding task vectors from 8 CLIP image-classification tasks gives one model at 91.2% normalized accuracy (98.9% for pairs), and negating a toxicity task vector reduces toxic generations with little loss of fluency.

relations.note: uniform soup is task arithmetic with lambda = 1/N
TIES replaces the plain sum by trim/elect/disjoint-mean

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2212.04089 (Ilharco, 2022); ICLR 2023 per arXiv comment. tau = theta_ft - theta_pre, theta_new = theta + lambda tau_new with lambda tuned on held-out validation data, negation and analogy tau_C + (tau_B - tau_A), 91.2% normalized accuracy for 8 tasks and 98.9% for pairs confirmed. HF add_weighted_adapter read on peft main (v0.21.1).
corrections: hf_peft_config: explained which combination_type reproduces task arithmetic on Delta W. 'svd' and 'cat' are exact (svd up to rank truncation). 'linear' mixes factors and adds cross terms, as the PEFT docstring warns.

relations: removed 'generalizes pem-arithmetic'. PEM addition acts on the (A, B) factors and creates cross terms B_1A_2 + B_2A_1, and its negation acts on one factor only, so PEM is not a special case of task arithmetic on Delta W. The inverse link 'pem-arithmetic builds-on task-arithmetic' remains.

methods.name: TIES-Merging
methods.full_name: TrIm, Elect Sign & Merge
methods.paper_title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='ties' | 'ties_svd', density=k, majority_sign_method='total' | 'frequency'); 'ties' trims and elects signs on the lora_A and lora_B factors separately, 'ties_svd' on the dense Delta W followed by SVD truncation; also IA3 vectors via merge_utils.ties
methods.formula_latex: \hat\tau_i=\operatorname{TopK}_{k\%}(\tau_i)\ (\text{trim});\quad \gamma^{p}=\operatorname{sgn}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{i}\hat\tau_i^{p}\Big)\ (\text{elect});\quad \tau_m^{p}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}^{p}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}^{p}}\hat\tau_i^{p},\ \mathcal{A}^{p}=\{i:\operatorname{sgn}(\hat\tau_i^{p})=\gamma^{p}\}\ (\text{disjoint merge});\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\,\tau_m
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(hyper-parameters }k\approx20\%,\ \lambda\approx1)
methods.locus: task vectors of full fine-tuning or of PEFT parameters (e.g. (IA)^3 vectors, LoRA factors in HF PEFT)
methods.structure: Coordinate-wise non-linear aggregation: magnitude sparsification, sign election by total mass, and a mean over agreeing non-zero entries only; not a linear combination of task vectors.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged task vector is added to the base weights once, giving a standard model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Merging interference comes from redundant small updates and sign conflicts; trimming small entries, electing one sign per parameter and averaging only agreeing values recovers much of the accuracy lost by plain averaging.
methods.results_note: With validation-tuned hyper-parameters, TIES outperforms averaging, Fisher merging, RegMean and Task Arithmetic across T5, ViT and (IA)^3-PEFT merges, in-domain and out-of-domain. Without a validation set, the fixed recipe (k = 20%, lambda = 1) is weaker than Task Arithmetic for the T5-base (IA)^3 merge (69.7 vs 73.2).

relations.note: operates on the same task vectors
DARE-TIES: random drop-and-rescale followed by TIES sign election

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2306.01708 (Yadav, 2023); NeurIPS 2023 per arXiv comment and papers.nips.cc. Trim top-k% by magnitude, sign election by total mass, disjoint mean over agreeing entries, theta = theta_init + lambda tau_m, and the no-validation recipe k = 20%, lambda = 1 confirmed (Alg. 1, Sec. 6). PEFT merge_utils.ties read on main.
corrections: hf_peft_config: added majority_sign_method='frequency' and noted that 'ties' acts on the LoRA factors, while 'ties_svd' acts on the dense delta, which matches the paper's per-parameter TIES.
results_note: qualified the claim. TIES beats all baselines only with validation-tuned hyper-parameters. Its no-validation recipe loses to Task Arithmetic on the (IA)^3 T5-base row of Table 1.
relations: removed 'builds-on ia3'. (IA)^3 is only one of the evaluation settings (the PEFT models being merged), not a component TIES depends on.

methods.name: DARE
methods.full_name: Drop And REscale
methods.paper_title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
methods.formula_latex: m_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\ \text{elementwise},\quad \hat\tau_i=\frac{(\mathbf{1}-m_i)\odot\tau_i}{1-p};\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\textstyle\sum_i\hat\tau_i\ (\text{DARE+TA})\ \text{or TIES on }\{\hat\tau_i\};\ \text{no training}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(drop rate }p\text{, up to }0.9\text{--}0.99)
methods.locus: delta parameters (fine-tuned minus pre-trained) of homologous SFT models; LoRA factors in HF PEFT
methods.structure: Random sparse coordinate mask with inverted-dropout rescaling 1/(1-p), which preserves the expectation of each delta and of its action on inputs; a pre-processing operator applied before any merge rule.
methods.mergeable_reason: Sparsified deltas are added back to the base weights, giving one ordinary model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: SFT deltas of language models are extremely redundant: randomly dropping 90-99% of them and rescaling the rest barely changes behaviour, and sparsified deltas of several homologous models interfere less when merged.
methods.results_note: DARE removes 90% or even 99% of delta parameters with little performance loss, and a DARE-merged 7B model ranked first among 7B models on the Open LLM Leaderboard at the time.

relations.note: commonly used as DARE-TIES
DARE+Task Arithmetic is the basic merge

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2311.03099 (Yu, 2023); ICML 2024 per arXiv comment and PMLR v235. Bernoulli(p) drop with 1/(1-p) rescaling, 90-99% drop rates and the top-ranked 7B merged model on the Open LLM Leaderboard confirmed. PEFT random_pruning keeps a fraction density = 1 - p and rescales by 1/density.

methods.name: AdaMerging
methods.full_name: Adaptive Model Merging
methods.paper_title: AdaMerging: Adaptive Model Merging for Multi-Task Learning
methods.formula_latex: \theta_m^{l}=\theta_0^{l}+\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i^{l}\,\tau_i^{l}\ \ (\text{layer-wise; task-wise uses one }\lambda_i\text{ per model});\quad \{\lambda\}=\arg\min_{\lambda}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{unlab}}_{\mathrm{test}}}H\big(f_{\theta_m(\lambda)}(x)\big),\ H=\text{prediction entropy};\ \text{task vectors frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\ \text{per layer (layer-wise) or }N\text{ in total (task-wise)}
methods.locus: task vectors of all layers (CLIP ViT image encoders in the paper)
methods.structure: Learned layer-wise linear combination of task vectors, fitted by test-time entropy minimization on unlabeled multi-task inputs.
methods.mergeable_reason: After learning the coefficients the merged weights form one ordinary model.
methods.identity_at_init: Coefficients initialized to the task-arithmetic default \lambda=0.3 (not an identity initialization).
methods.key_idea: Merging coefficients matter a lot; they can be learned per task and per layer without labels by minimizing the entropy of the merged model's predictions on unlabeled test inputs.
methods.results_note: Merging eight ViT task models, AdaMerging improves average accuracy by about 11% over Task Arithmetic and generalizes better to unseen tasks and distribution shift.

relations.note: learned per-layer coefficients instead of one global lambda
also applied on top of TIES task vectors
both fit merging coefficients post hoc (AdaMerging by test-time entropy gradients, LoraHub by gradient-free few-shot search); conceptual pairing, neither paper benchmarks the other

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2310.02575 (Yang, 2023); ICLR 2024 per arXiv comment and proceedings.iclr.cc. Task-wise and layer-wise coefficients, entropy minimization on unlabeled test data, initialization lambda = 0.3 (App., 'initialize all coefficients to 0.3') and the ~11% gain over Task Arithmetic confirmed.
corrections: relations: marked the lorahub link as conceptual. Neither paper compares against the other.

methods.name: TSV-Merge
methods.full_name: Task Singular Vectors Merge (TSV-M) and Compress (TSV-C)
methods.paper_title: Task Singular Vectors: Reducing Task Interference in Model Merging
methods.formula_latex: \Delta_i=U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}\ (\text{keep top }1/N\text{ components});\ U=[U_1|\cdots|U_N],\ \Sigma=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_N),\ V=[V_1|\cdots|V_N];\ U=P_UD_UQ_U^{\top}\Rightarrow U_\perp=P_UQ_U^{\top}\ (\text{same for }V);\ W=W_0+\alpha\,U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one scaling }\alpha\text{; the paper finds }\alpha=1\text{ best, so no tuning is needed)}
methods.locus: per-layer task matrices of all weight matrices (ViT CLIP encoders in the paper)
methods.structure: Per-layer low-rank truncation of each task matrix, then orthogonalization (whitening, equivalently orthogonal Procrustes) of the concatenated singular-vector bases to remove cross-task overlap measured by the Singular Task Interference \|(U^{\top}U-I)\Sigma(V^{\top}V-I)\|_1.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged matrix is added once to the pre-trained weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Layer task matrices are low-rank, so each can be kept as its top singular vectors; interference appears as overlap between different tasks' singular vectors and can be removed by orthogonalizing the stacked bases before summation.
methods.results_note: TSV-C compresses task matrices to 10% of their size while retaining 99% of accuracy, and TSV-M significantly outperforms prior merging methods on 8/14/20-task ViT benchmarks.

relations.note: replaces flat task vectors with per-layer SVD structure
both merge in an SVD basis; KnOTS shares U Sigma across LoRAs, TSV orthogonalizes per-task bases

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2412.00081 (Gargiulo, 2024); CVPR 2025 per arXiv comment and IEEE DOI 10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.01742. Per-layer SVD truncation to a 1/T share per task, whitening X(X^T X)^{-1/2} = PQ^T (Procrustes, Prop. 1), the STI score (Eq. 6), and TSV-C's 10% size with 99% accuracy confirmed.
corrections: trainable_params: added that alpha = 1 works best in the paper (Sec. 6.3, Fig. 7), so TSV-M needs no coefficient tuning.

methods.name: KnOTS
methods.full_name: Knowledge Orientation Through SVD
methods.paper_title: Model merging with SVD to tie the Knots
methods.formula_latex: \big[\Delta W^{(1)}\ \cdots\ \Delta W^{(N)}\big]=U\Sigma\,\big[V^{(1)};\dots;V^{(N)}\big]^{\top}\ \ (\Delta W^{(i)}=B_iA_i);\quad V^{(m)}=\operatorname{Merge}\big(V^{(1)},\dots,V^{(N)}\big)\ (\text{TA, TIES, DARE},\dots);\quad W=W_0+U\Sigma\,V^{(m)\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(data-free, gradient-free)}
methods.locus: LoRA-adapted attention projections (q, k, v, o) of ViT-B/32, ViT-L/16 and Llama3-8B LoRA models in the paper (rank 16)
methods.structure: Joint SVD of the column-concatenated LoRA updates: a shared orthonormal output basis U\Sigma (rank \le N r) and task-specific input-side factors V^{(i)}; any existing merge rule is applied in this aligned coordinate system.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged update U Sigma V^(m)T is a dense matrix added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates of different tasks are much less aligned than full fine-tuning deltas; re-expressing them in a common SVD basis aligns them so that standard merging rules stop destroying each other's information.
methods.results_note: KnOTS improves LoRA merging by up to 4.3% across vision and language benchmarks, including a new joint-task benchmark for general models.

relations.note: TIES/DARE/TA are applied to the aligned V factors
designed for merging LoRA-finetuned models
SVD-based merging

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.19735 (Stoica, 2024); ICLR 2025 confirmed in proceedings.iclr.cc 2025. Column-wise concatenation, SVD = U Sigma [V^(1);...;V^(n)]^T, merge of the V's, and Delta W = U Sigma V^(merged)T added to W_0 (Eq. 1-2), plus 'up to 4.3%', confirmed. Code repo exists.
corrections: locus: specified the q/k/v/o attention placement and rank 16 used in the experiments (Sec. 5.1).

methods.name: PEM Arithmetic
methods.full_name: Composing parameter-efficient modules with arithmetic operations
methods.paper_title: Composing Parameter-Efficient Modules with Arithmetic Operations
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='linear'): PEFT scales each factor by sqrt(|w_i| * scaling_i) and puts the sign on lora_A only, so weights w_i = lambda_i^2 reproduce PEM addition and a negative weight reproduces PEM negation; IA3Model.add_weighted_adapter gives (IA)^3 addition, but the affine negation l -> 2 - l is not built in
methods.formula_latex: \theta^{\mathrm{add}}=\lambda\theta^{(1)}\oplus(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}:=\lambda\theta^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}\ \ (\text{component-wise on }(A,B)\text{ or on }l);\quad \ominus\theta_{\mathrm{LoRA}}=\{A,-B\}\ \Rightarrow\ \Delta h=BAx\mapsto-\Delta h;\quad \ominus l_{(IA)^3}=\mathbf{2}-l;\ \text{e.g. domain transfer }\theta^{(1)}\ominus\theta^{(2)}\oplus\theta^{(3)};\ \text{no training}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(weight }\lambda\text{ tuned on validation)}
methods.locus: LoRA factors or (IA)^3 scaling vectors of modules trained from the same base model
methods.structure: Addition is defined on module parameters (for LoRA (A_1+A_2),(B_1+B_2), which creates cross terms B_1A_2+B_2A_1), whereas negation is defined through the induced hidden-state change \Delta h: negate only B for LoRA, l\mapsto 2-l for (IA)^3, because negating both factors leaves BA unchanged.
methods.mergeable_reason: The composed module is again a LoRA/(IA)^3 module, which can be folded into the base weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: PEFT modules trained from one base model can be composed by weight-space arithmetic; the subtle part is negation, which must flip the module's effect on hidden states rather than its raw parameters.
methods.results_note: Arithmetic compositions of LoRA/(IA)^3 modules (RoBERTa-base, T5-base) beat the individual modules for distribution generalization, multi-tasking, unlearning and domain transfer, and LoRA negation detoxifies Alpaca-LoRA.

relations.note: task arithmetic restricted to PEFT parameters with a corrected negation
same factor-wise linear composition; LoraHub searches the weights
composes LoRA modules
composes (IA)^3 modules with l -> 2 - l negation

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2306.14870 (Zhang, 2023); NeurIPS 2023 per arXiv comment and papers.nips.cc. Addition is component-wise on module parameters; negation is {A, -B} for LoRA (Eq. 6) and l_neg = 2 - l for (IA)^3 (Eq. 7). The PDF footnote gives the code at github.com/hkust-nlp/PEM_composition (the arXiv comment's SJTU-LIT URL also resolves).
corrections: hf_peft_config: explained how PEFT's sqrt-weight convention maps onto PEM (weights lambda^2, sign on one factor). Added that IA3Model.add_weighted_adapter covers (IA)^3 addition only, not the 2 - l negation.

methods.name: AdapterSoup
methods.full_name: AdapterSoup: weight averaging of domain adapters
methods.paper_title: AdapterSoup: Weight Averaging to Improve Generalization of Pretrained Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta_{\mathrm{soup}}=\tfrac{1}{l}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\theta_i,\ |\mathcal{S}|=l\le k;\quad y=f\big(x;\theta_m,\theta_{\mathrm{soup}}\big);\ \mathcal{S}\text{ chosen by sentence-BERT similarity or domain clustering on a little novel-domain text};\ \text{PLM }\theta_m\text{ and all adapters frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{for the novel domain (}k\text{ domain adapters are trained beforehand, each a bottleneck adapter of }\approx2rd\text{ per layer)}
methods.locus: Bapna and Firat (2019)-style bottleneck adapters (bottleneck size 64) in every Transformer layer of GPT-2
methods.structure: Uniform average (a model soup) of a retrieved subset of adapter parameter vectors; one averaged adapter is executed at test time.
methods.mergeable_reason: The soup collapses the selected adapters into one adapter, so inference costs a single adapter. That adapter is a nonlinear bottleneck module and cannot fold into W_0. The same recipe applied to LoRAs (mentioned only as future work) would be foldable.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free combination of trained adapters).
methods.key_idea: For an unseen domain, rather than picking one related-domain adapter, average the weights of several selected domain adapters to obtain ensemble-like gains at the cost of a single adapter.
methods.results_note: On 10 held-out web domains with GPT-2, AdapterSoup with clustering-based selection gives the best average out-of-domain perplexity among single-adapter-cost methods.

relations.note: model soup restricted to adapter parameters
averages serial bottleneck adapters of the Houlsby family (Bapna and Firat 2019 variant)
LoraHub learns signed weights instead of uniform averaging

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2302.07027 (Chronopoulou, 2023); Findings of EACL 2023 confirmed (ACL Anthology 2023.findings-eacl.153). Uniform weight average of l selected domain adapters (Eq. 1), selection by sentence-BERT similarity or clustering, clustering best on novel domains, GPT-2 backbone confirmed. No official code link found.
corrections: locus: named the adapter architecture used (Bapna and Firat 2019, bottleneck 64; Sec. 4), not generic 'bottleneck adapters'.
mergeable: 'conditional' -> 'no'. The averaged modules in the paper are nonlinear bottleneck adapters, which cannot fold into W_0. The soup does give single-adapter inference cost.
mergeable_reason: rewritten to match the 'no' verdict.
relations: houlsby-adapter note now names the actual Bapna and Firat variant.

methods.name: LoraHub
methods.full_name: LoraHub: dynamic LoRA composition
methods.paper_title: LoraHub: Efficient Cross-Task Generalization via Dynamic LoRA Composition
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iB_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iA_i\Big),\ \ w\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\ (\text{signed});\quad w^{\star}=\arg\min_{w}\ \mathcal{L}_{Q}(w)+\alpha\textstyle\sum_i|w_i|\ \text{by gradient-free CMA-ES (Nevergrad Shiwa)};\ W=W_0+\Delta W;\ \text{base model and all }(A_i,B_i)\text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\ \text{scalars in total (e.g. }N=20\text{ randomly sampled LoRAs), shared by all layers}
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices of the base model (Flan-T5 in the paper)
methods.structure: Element-wise linear combination of the factor matrices (a product of sums, which introduces cross terms B_iA_j), with one global coefficient per module found by black-box optimization on a few examples.
methods.mergeable_reason: The composed LoRA has fixed weights and can be merged into W_0 like any LoRA.

papers.title: Modular Deep Learning
papers.claim: Surveys modular deep learning as parameter-efficient modules whose computation is conditionally routed to a subset of modules and then aggregated, unifying adapters, mixture-of-experts, composition and hypernetwork threads under computation / routing / aggregation functions.
papers.relevance: Its module-routing-aggregation decomposition is the informal signature that a categorical treatment of PEFT composition formalizes: modules as morphisms, routing as selection among parallel morphisms, aggregation as a monoidal combination.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2302.11529 (Pfeiffer, 2023); TMLR (Dec 2023, Survey Certification) confirmed in the TMLR accepted-paper list. Claim matches the abstract (computation, routing and aggregation functions).

papers.title: Task Arithmetic in the Tangent Space: Improved Editing of Pre-Trained Models
papers.claim: Weight disentanglement (distinct weight directions controlling separate, localized regions of function space) is the property that makes task arithmetic work; fine-tuning in the linearized (tangent) regime amplifies it and improves task addition and negation.
papers.relevance: Identifies when the map from task vectors to functions behaves like a linear map (a homomorphism of the additive structure), which is the precondition for treating merging as vector-space arithmetic.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.12827 (Ortiz-Jimenez, 2023); NeurIPS 2023 confirmed (arXiv journal-ref, papers.nips.cc). Weight-disentanglement claim matches the paper.

papers.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
papers.claim: After accounting for permutation symmetries of hidden units, loss landscapes often contain nearly a single basin; aligning one model's units to another's permutation lets independently trained models be merged by linear interpolation.
papers.relevance: Shows that merging is well-defined only up to a symmetry group acting on weights; LoRA factorizations carry an analogous GL(r)/permutation gauge (cf. LoRA-LEGO, KnOTS), so adapters are naturally objects up to isomorphism.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2209.04836 (Ainsworth, 2022); ICLR 2023 per Semantic Scholar venue metadata. Claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
papers.claim: Networks become stable to SGD noise early in training: from then on, runs that share a starting point end in minima connected by a linear path of low loss.
papers.relevance: Grounds the shared-basin assumption behind all merging of models or adapters fine-tuned from one pre-trained point, i.e. why deltas from a common base can be treated as vectors in one affine chart.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1912.05671 (Frankle, 2019); ICML 2020 per arXiv comment ('Published in ICML 2020'). Claim matches.

papers.title: Model Merging in LLMs, MLLMs, and Beyond: Methods, Theories, Applications and Opportunities
papers.claim: Proposes a taxonomy of model merging methods (pre-merging alignment, during-merging weighting/subspace/routing methods), reviews the theory, and surveys applications in LLMs, multimodal models and more than ten machine-learning subfields.
papers.relevance: The most complete map of the merging half of this family; its taxonomy is a reference point to check against a categorical classification of merge operators.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2408.07666 (Yang, 2024); published in ACM Computing Surveys (DOI 10.1145/3787849, 2026). The taxonomy claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: What Matters for Model Merging at Scale?
papers.claim: Merging experts fine-tuned from 1B-64B models shows that merging works better from strong (instruction-tuned) base models, larger models merge more easily and more experts, merged models generalize better, and different merging methods behave very similarly at large scale.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that at scale the choice of merge operator matters less than the base point, suggesting that the algebra of merging becomes closer to linear near strong pre-trained models.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.03617 (Yadav, 2024); TMLR 2025. The 1B-64B scale, up to 8 experts, and the five findings in the claim match the abstract.

papers.claim: A small network can generate the weights of a larger main network and be trained end-to-end, acting as a relaxed form of weight sharing; generated non-shared LSTM weights reach near state-of-the-art results on sequence modelling.
papers.relevance: Adapter generators (HyperFormer, HyperDreamBooth, Text-to-LoRA, Doc-to-LoRA, DnD) are hypernetworks: maps from a conditioning space (task, image, text, document) into the space of adapters.

papers.claim: An autoencoder plus a latent diffusion model trained on checkpoints can generate new, high-performing parameters for a subset of network weights that are not mere memorized copies of the training checkpoints.
papers.relevance: Establishes generative modelling directly over parameter (adapter) space, the line that prompt-conditioned LoRA generators such as Drag-and-Drop LLMs extend.

notes: Scope: 42 methods across five sub-families: (i) training-free / post-hoc merging of deltas or adapters (model-soups, fisher-merging, regmean, task-arithmetic, ties-merging, dare, adamerging, tsv-merge, knots, pem-arithmetic, adaptersoup, lorahub, lora-soups, lora-lego, ziplora, mix-of-show, orthogonal-adaptation, multi-lora-composition); (ii) learned composition and mixtures (adapterfusion, adamix, polytropon, mhr, smear, mov, loramoe, moelora, mole, mixlora, x-lora, hydralora, lily); (iii) post-hoc routing and retrieval over adapter libraries (phatgoose, arrow, loraretriever, lora-flow); (iv) multi-adapter serving (s-lora, punica); (v) adapter generation by hypernetworks (hyperformer, hyperdreambooth, text-to-lora, drag-and-drop-llms, doc-to-lora). Seed checks: all 21 seeds exist and belong. 'MoELoRA' is ambiguous: we used Liu et al. (SIGIR 2024, arXiv 2310.18339, spelled MOELoRA); Luo et al. 2024 ('MoELoRA: Contrastive Learning Guided Mixture of Experts...', arXiv 2402.12851) is a different, less-cited method that we did not verify. Polytropon's arXiv title ('Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning') differs from the EACL 2023 title used here. LoRAMoE's published title says 'Alleviating' (arXiv: 'Alleviate'). Key algebraic distinction for the theory: 'product of sums' factor mixing (LoraHub, Polytropon/MHR, Arrow-paper, PEM addition, HF PEFT combination_type='linear') creates cross terms B_iA_j, whereas 'sum of products' / rank-concatenation (LoRA Soups CAT, HF 'cat', LoRA-LEGO with k=sum r_i, Doc-to-LoRA chunking, X-LoRA, LoRA-Flow, PHATGOOSE, HF Arrow implementation) is the direct sum along the rank axis. HF PEFT's Arrow mixes expert outputs while the Arrow paper mixes factors. HF PEFT: add_weighted_adapter supports svd, linear, cat, ties, ties_svd, dare_linear, dare_ties, dare_*_svd, magnitude_prune(_svd); negative weights are applied to one factor only (PEM-style negation). PEFT also implements XLoraConfig, PolyConfig (Poly and MHR), ArrowConfig (+GenKnowSub) inside LoraConfig, and LilyConfig. Not in PEFT: MoLE, LoRAMoE, MixLoRA, HydraLoRA, MOELoRA, LoraHub (separate library), CAT with learned weights, serving systems. Uncertainties: MoLE gate parameter shapes are as written in the paper (Eq. 9-10: e in R^{(N L d) x N} over flattened block outputs), now checked; identity-at-init for LoRAMoE, MOELoRA, MixLoRA and HydraLoRA is confirmed from the official code (zero-initialized B), not the papers; Orthogonal Adaptation's trainable-factor init remains unstated; MixLoRA has no formal venue found (arXiv); 'What Matters for Model Merging at Scale?' is TMLR 2025 (verified); Doc-to-LoRA hypernetwork size (309M) is stated in the paper (Sec. 5) and on the Sakana project page. Skipped as lower-uptake or out of PEFT focus: Model Breadcrumbs, EMR-Merging, Twin-Merging, WEMoE, Consensus/TALL masks, Iso-C/Iso-CTS, K-LoRA, further LoRA-MoE variants (AdaMoLE, MoLA, SiRA, MoSLoRA), dLoRA and CaraServe serving systems, HINT and HyperTuning hypernetworks, ATTEMPT (covered in the prompts family).
verification_summary: Adversarially verified on 2026-10-01: 42 methods and 8 papers, none dropped. All 50 arXiv ids were batch-checked against the arXiv API: titles, first authors and first-version years all match (two titles differ only in the published versions: Polytropon at EACL 2023 and LoRAMoE at ACL 2024). Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments, ACL Anthology, PMLR (v235, v267), proceedings.iclr.cc (2024, 2025), papers.nips.cc, proceedings.mlsys.org 2024, the TMLR accepted list, Crossref DOIs (ECCV, CVPR, SIGIR, APL ML, ACM CSUR, Findings ACL 2025) and Semantic Scholar. Doc-to-LoRA's ICML 2026 venue comes from the official README citation. Every formula and parameter count was checked against the arXiv PDF text. Official code was read for initialization (LoRAMoE, MOELoRA, MixLoRA, HydraLoRA) and for HydraLoRA's router shape. HF PEFT claims were checked against huggingface/peft main (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29): lora/model.py add_weighted_adapter, utils/merge_utils.py, ia3/model.py, poly, lily, xlora, lora/arrow.py and the docs. 61 corrections. Key fixes: merging-at-scale venue arXiv -> TMLR 2025; model-merging-survey -> ACM Computing Surveys 2026; MoLE code_url (paper link 404s); AdapterSoup mergeable conditional -> no; trainable counts for AdaMix ((M+1)rd), HyperFormer (paper Sec. 4.1 formula), MoV, MoLE, X-LoRA, SMEAR, T2L (exact 55.25M/34.28M/4.92M) and D2L; Orthogonal Adaptation crosstalk condition; Lily PEFT router pooling; HydraLoRA router shape; D2L locus (MLP down-projection). Eleven unjustified relations fixed (8 deleted, 3 retyped): TA->PEM, TIES->ia3, OrthAdapt->TA, SMEAR->MoV, SMEAR->PHATGOOSE, PHATGOOSE->SMEAR, LoraRetriever->S-LoRA, D2L->LoRA Soups deleted; LoRA Soups<->LoRA-LEGO and LoRA-Flow->LoraHub retyped to competes-with. Cross-file differences left for reconciliation: AdaMix mergeable (here 'conditional', since the paper reports adapter and LoRA forms; adapters.json says 'no'), and T2L, DnD and D2L mergeable (here 'yes', since a generated adapter is a plain LoRA; frontier.json says 'conditional').
